title: Mississippi Pot Roast for the Crew
displayTitle: Mississippi Pot Roast for the Crew
seoTitle: Mississippi Pot Roast for the Crew | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Tangy pepperoncini roast made for a busy shift
subtitle: Tangy pepperoncini roast made for a busy shift
description: Chuck roast cooks low and slow with pepperoncini, ranch seasoning, and beef gravy.

steps.title: Morning start
steps.instruction: At breakfast, place roast in a 6-to-8-quart slow cooker and wash hands after handling raw beef.

steps.title: Season roast
steps.instruction: Sprinkle ranch seasoning over the roast and add broth and pepperoncini with some brine.

steps.title: Set cooker
steps.instruction: Cover and cook on low for 8 hours; do not repeatedly lift the lid because heat escapes.

steps.title: Check liquid
steps.instruction: At mid-shift, confirm there is liquid around the roast and add broth if the pot looks dry.

steps.title: Cook potatoes
steps.instruction: Near dinner, boil potatoes until fork-tender and steam carrots until tender-crisp.

steps.title: Test tenderness
steps.instruction: Slide a fork into the roast; it should twist easily without forcing.

steps.title: Shred beef
steps.instruction: Move roast to a tray and shred with two forks, discarding large pieces of fat.

steps.title: Finish juices
steps.instruction: Skim excess fat from the cooker juices, then return shredded beef and stir.

steps.title: Hold safely
steps.instruction: Set slow cooker to warm only after the beef is above 165°F; keep it above 140°F.

steps.title: Serve dinner
steps.instruction: Spoon juicy beef over mashed potatoes with carrots and pepperoncini on the side.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-cook: turn off direct heat and cover Chuck roast — hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven, never below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Log hold time on the pan with a grease pencil. If tones drop after service, cover hot food and keep sides on low heat or ice as appropriate. On return, spot-check proteins at safe internal temp before reopening the line.

steps.title: Pack down leftovers safely
steps.instruction: Cool Chuck roast and hot components in shallow hotel pans within two hours — deep pots stay in the danger zone too long. Label with date; reheat proteins to 165°F minimum before second shift. Store cold components separately so textures survive overnight.

proTips: Use two slow cookers if yours cannot safely hold the volume.
Pepperoncini add tang, not overwhelming heat.
Keep beef covered with liquid on warm.
tonightSpread: Set hot components closest to the crew; cold crunch and toppings at the far end of the line.
Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a run.
leftovers: Cool Chuck roast in shallow pans within two hours; label with date and reheat to 165°F before second shift.
Store cold sides separately — hot and cold stacked overnight ruins texture.
whyCrewsLikeIt: The slow cooker tolerates interrupted schedules and holds shredded beef well.
mealPrepNotes: Make-ahead: season roast overnight. Storage: refrigerate for 3 days. Reheating: reheat shredded beef and juices to 165°F.
substitutions: Use beef stew meat for chuck roast.
Use Italian seasoning for ranch mix.
